questions.prompt: How much should the first extraction move into the shared UI kit?
questions.context: We have agreed to a shared UI home with agent documentation and examples. Outcome and grill-form remain separate workflows. The common pieces include styling, Markdown/tables/diagrams, choices, Notes/images, action buttons and feedback status. Grill-form also has specialized interactive previews and region comments.
questions.recommendation: Move the common pieces and migrate both skills in this pass. Keep specialized preview/comment tools local until a concrete reuse need appears.

options.label: All existing UI, including previews and region comments
Styling and rich-content rendering first; controls later

questions.prompt: How much visual variation should workflow skills have?
questions.context: Shared components can still drift if each skill adds its own overrides. Page composition can differ without changing the appearance or behavior of a shared control.
questions.recommendation: Use shared defaults with a few named variants, such as compact and regular. Changes to a shared control belong in the kit.

options.label: One fixed appearance for every shared component
Let each workflow override component styles freely

questions.prompt: Which Notes experience should become the shared default?
questions.context: Grill-form currently keeps pasted images as clickable chips inside the text. Outcome keeps text references with separate image thumbnails. These previews illustrate that difference; they are not functioning editors. Either choice keeps pasted images, previewing, draft recovery and optional Notes.
questions.recommendation: Use inline image chips, as in grill-form. Text and image references stay together, and its editor already handles editing and undo around the chips.

options.label: Keep both as documented editor variants

questions.prompt: Should ordinary skill use require an extra assembly tool such as Node.js?
questions.context: Fungi only serves assets beneath the opened page’s directory. It cannot directly import a sibling skill’s files. We need to handle that packaging centrally. Prepared distributions can avoid extra runtime tools; a per-session assembly helper adds a runtime prerequisite.
questions.recommendation: Keep ordinary use to Fungi plus the installed skill files. Handle assembly during development or distribution, with one maintained source for components.

options.label: No extra runtime tools; provide prepared interfaces (Recommended)
A local assembly helper at launch is acceptable

questions.prompt: What should an agent do when it needs a reusable control the kit does not have?
questions.context: This concerns controls such as a new picker or editor. One-off report illustrations and the designs being reviewed can still be authored as content. The policy should prevent copied controls from drifting across future skills.
questions.recommendation: Add generally reusable controls to the shared kit, with a small example and documentation, then consume them from the workflow.

options.label: Add reusable controls to the kit first (Recommended)
Build locally; promote when a second workflow needs it
Ask me before adding a new reusable control
